title: SEIS AI Lab robot, design studies v001: compact and slim
tagline: Two rigged white-box-head robot mascots for the SEIS AI Lab, built from primitives in Blender. A design study, not a final model.
stats: 2 models · 135 meshes each · 51,536 (compact) and 51,984 (slim) triangles · 7 materials in the GLB · 17 bones each · 1.68 m (compact) and 2.08 m (slim) tall with antenna · Blender 5.1.2
description: Two takes on the same mascot: a compact, boxy lead design (large rectangular head, short legs, broad feet) and a slimmer, long-legged comparison. Both have a white box head with two raised black oval eyes and a thin black waveform mouth, a red 6 modelled as real mesh on the chest, white/gray/black parts with red accents, a 17-bone forward-kinematics skeleton and two mouth shape keys (Speaking, Emphasis). They are editable models made from primitives; the supplied drawing's distressed ink texture was not reproduced. This is a design study, not a final model. The source says both still need Bear's aesthetic review.

views.title: Compact, three-quarter
views.text: The lead design: a white box head wider than the torso, raised oval eyes, a thin zig-zag mouth, a red 6, short legs and slab feet. Clean and toy-like; the 6 and the waveform are what tie it to the reference.

views.title: Compact, front
views.text: Dead-on front. The head is almost as wide as the whole figure and the legs are stubby, so the body looks like an afterthought under the head. Antenna is a simple stalk with a red ball.

views.title: Compact, side
views.text: The round side port is a plain disc; the supplied boxy reference has a deeper lens-like fitting there. Torso is shallow front to back.

views.title: Compact, back
views.text: A blank white head and a back panel with slot lines. Nothing here comes from a reference; it is invented filler.

views.title: Compact, top
views.text: Top of the head with the antenna base. Useful only to confirm the head is a rounded box.

views.title: Compact, silent
views.text: Mouth shape key set to silent: the lower face is blank white. Eyes still read, but the face is mostly empty.

views.title: Compact, bent pose
views.text: Head tilted and one arm raised using the FK rig. It proves the joints turn as rigid parts; there is no skinning, so every limb is a stiff block.

views.title: Compact, wireframe
views.text: The mesh is clean primitives (about 51,500 triangles) with many small joint parts; nothing is sculpted.

views.title: Slim, three-quarter
views.text: Same head and face on longer limbs. Closer to the supplied drawing's lanky proportions than the compact one, but legs are thin straight tubes and the feet are flat slabs rather than the drawing's rounded shoes.

views.title: Slim, front
views.text: The chest box and 6 are small under a large head. Arms hang straight with the same blocky hands as the compact version.

views.title: Slim, side
views.text: Very thin in profile; the head looks like it is balanced on a stick.

views.title: Slim, back
views.text: Same blank head and slotted back panel as the compact model.

views.title: Slim, silent
views.text: Silent mouth state on the slim body.

views.title: Slim, bent pose
views.text: The same bent-pose test on the slim rig. Reads as stiff mannequin posing, not character acting.

compares.title: Supplied drawing vs compact (three-quarter)
compares.text: Left: the supplied approved-waveform drawing. Right: the compact render. The head box, oval eyes, waveform mouth, red 6 and red-dot joints are carried over. It falls short on everything that gives the drawing life: the drawing's torso is a rounded block with a lean body and long legs, the compact is a squat figure with a huge head; the drawing has rounded shoes and an open gesturing hand, the render has slab feet and a stiff relaxed arm; the ink-wear texture is absent. Likeness: recognisably the same idea, but a clean toy version, and the proportions are the biggest miss.

compares.title: Supplied drawing vs slim (three-quarter)
compares.text: Left: the same supplied drawing. Right: the slim render. Limb length and overall height are nearer the drawing than in the compact model. Still missing: the rounded torso, the rounded shoes, the ink texture and the raised hand. The slim legs and arms are straighter and more uniform than the drawing's articulated joints. Likeness: closer in proportion than compact, still a simplified primitive version.

compares.title: Supplied boxy reference vs compact (bent pose)
compares.text: Left: the supplied boxy-body reference (a dark, stylised image of a tilted box head on a small cylindrical body). Right: the compact bent-pose render. The tilted box head, small body and two-antenna idea match loosely; the reference has two antennas, a camera-lens fitting on the head side, round chunky torso and arm cylinders and a worn black finish. The render is white, has one antenna, a flat disc port, and a rectangular torso. Likeness: shares only the head-to-body ratio and attitude.

blend_note: Saved by Blender 5.1.2; it has never been opened in Blender 4.2, so 4.2 compatibility is untested (use Blender 5.1 or later to match the build).
glb_note: Both GLBs use flat material colours only: no textures or images are embedded (0 textures, 7 materials each). They include the 17-bone skeleton and the Speaking and Emphasis morph targets, with no animation clips. The camera, lights and floor are not in the GLBs.

built_by.builder: Codex (OpenAI). Builder identified from Codex session logs on this machine dated 2026-10-18, not from a label in the folder; no product or model version is stated in the files.
built_by.method: Scripted: one Blender Python script (scripts/build_robot.py) builds either variant from primitives in a fresh background Blender. No sculpting and no AI image-to-3D. The source lists no numbered render-versus-reference rounds; it records one headless build per variant, a render pass, and mechanical checks. The compare images in this folder were made afterwards for this page, by eye.
built_by.tools: Blender 5.1.2 (confirmed by my scene count); Khronos glTF Blender I/O v5.1.20; the source's own validator (zero errors, zero warnings, both variants); Godot 4.7.2 import test recorded by the source (both pass). The source says the guide named Blender 5.2 LTS but 5.1.2 was what was installed.

limitations: This is a design study, not a final model.
The compact is the source's "lead design" label, not a human decision recorded in the folder.
Proportions differ from the supplied drawing (huge head on a squat body in the compact); the drawing's distressed ink texture, rounded shoes and open gesturing hand are not reproduced.
Fingers are rigid parts of each hand, not rigged individually. No IK, control rig, walk cycle or animation; the rig is simple FK with every part fully weighted to one bone.
The mouth uses two discrete shape-key controls; no speech sync, no sound is attached.

Counts: my count_scene run on the .blend files reports 136 mesh objects and 51,538 / 51,986 triangles, which is the source's 135 meshes and 51,536 / 51,984 triangles plus a 2-triangle floor plane; the .blend also shows 8 materials against 7 in the GLB (the extra is presentation-only).
Height figures (1.6815 m and 2.0765 m with antenna) come from the source's own audit; my count cannot give them because of the large floor plane.
Verification of Godot import and the GLB round-trip is as recorded by the source; I did not re-run it.
build_notes:
## What it is

Two robots built in one pass from one script, `scripts/build_robot.py`: **compact** (lead design) and **slim** (comparison). The compact version follows a boxy-body reference; the slim keeps the longer limbs of the earlier white mascot (the source's wording). Both share the face, materials and rig.

## What I measured

From `scripts/count_scene.py` run on each .blend (Blender 5.1.2): compact 136 mesh objects, 51,538 triangles, 8 materials, 1 armature, 17 bones, 1 camera, 3 lights. Slim 136 mesh objects, 51,986 triangles, 8 materials, 1 armature, 17 bones, 1 camera, 3 lights. Raw output is in `reports/scene-counts-*.json`. The two extra triangles and one extra mesh over the source's figures are the studio floor plane.

Glb inspection (read from the glTF JSON): 0 images, 0 textures, 7 materials, 1 skin and 0 animations in each GLB.

## What the source reports (not re-run by me)

- Compact: 135 meshes, 51,536 triangles, 7 materials, 0 textures, 17 bones, one root, size 0.878 x 0.619 x 1.6815 m. Slim: 135 meshes, 51,984 triangles, 7 materials, 17 bones, size 0.838 x 0.599 x 2.0765 m. Design-study budget 60,000 triangles per robot.
- Walker validator: zero errors and zero warnings for both. GLB export and re-import: mesh, triangle, bone counts and bounds match.
- Godot 4.7.2 import test: both pass (one 17-bone skeleton, 135 meshes, Speaking/Emphasis morphs reachable).
- Logs and JSON in `reports/` (paths made relative for this repository).

## Controls

Select `SEIS_Compact_Rig` (or `SEIS_Slim_Rig`) and enter Pose Mode: head, torso, arms, wrists, hips, knees and feet can be posed. On the mouth object, `Speaking` 0 hides the waveform and 1 shows it; `Emphasis` adds amplitude. The model opens in a speaking state.

## Method notes

Built headless with the installed Blender; no live Blender MCP connection and no paid generation services were used (the source says so). The scripts were copied with absolute paths replaced by placeholders. `scripts/build_robot.py` loads the Lato Bold font from a path outside this repository to make the 6; edit that path to rebuild.

## Files copied from the source

Both .blend files, both GLBs, 16 renders (PNG), the build, render, validator and round-trip reports, the scripts, and the two supplied reference images in `references/`. Not copied: the Godot verification project, `.blend1` backups, review.html.
